video_title: Steve Nash Called It Quits After Playing Steph Curry

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on his final years with the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: My last two years with the Lakers, my second game with the Lakers, I bumped knees in Dame's first game

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Nash
text_blocks.text: When he came in the league, I still felt like the big brother. I still feel like I got the upper hand. Then he started becoming who he is and the pendulum shifted. My last two years with the Lakers, my second game with the Lakers, I bumped knees in Dame's first game with Dame and broke my tib-fib joint on the inside. It's where the nerve goes. I already had nerve stuff and I was never the same. I spent two years working out twice a day just to try to overcome it.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on playing through injury against the Warriors
quotes.excerpt: I'm guarding Steph. I think they put up like 50 in the first quarter.
quotes.quote: We went to play these guys preseason in Ontario, California. I'm guarding Steph. I think they put up like 50 in the first quarter. Maybe it was 45, but it felt like a 50 piece. He's running everywhere. I'm back is broke, everything is jacked. I couldn't have stopped him if I was 100 percent. I'm dragging around, Stevie Curry's putting me in every action. I'm looking over at Steve like, are you kidding me? We know he's over there smiling too. Alvin Gentry over there laughing at me. I'm like, no, no, no, I was just trying to see what you got. Man, literally like three more, four more days of thinking on it, I was like, yeah, I think it's time.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on the influence of Reggie Miller and Steve Nash
quotes.excerpt: Reggie makes so much sense and is terrifying to competitors like myself

text_blocks.speaker: LeBron James
text_blocks.text: You mentioned Steve and you mentioned Reggie. Obviously, Reggie makes so much sense and is terrifying to competitors like myself and all the competition over the years. What made you kind of watch those guys from the beginning?

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen Curry
text_blocks.text: My rookie year, we played in a preseason game outside in Palm Springs at Indian Wells. It was my first time I actually seen him on the court to the point of inspiration. I still do some of your, when you're in the starting line or the national anthem, the line, you still do like the little leg stuff. I still do it.

quotes.speaker: Stephen Curry
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry on his father's advice to shoot more
quotes.excerpt: My dad had to actually tell me to shoot more because I was a pass first type of point guard.
quotes.quote: Growing up, I knew I was a pass first type of point guard. My dad had to actually tell me to shoot more because I was a pass first type of point guard. I always just love the creativity. It felt like we had similar statures where as a point guard, being able to handle, being in the trees, getting the ball where you needed to, you saw angles that didn't even make sense. Your change of speed, you can control the tempo, got everybody involved. There was just something fun about that.

quotes.speaker: Stephen Curry
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry on his father's shooting form
quotes.excerpt: He had the high arc and release too. I couldn't get that.
quotes.quote: Every video you see of him, he's sitting in the corner, one dribble, and then the quick release. He had the high arc and release too. I couldn't get that. So it was almost comparison and contrast of I want to be a great shooter, I want to have a quick release, but I also have to own my own form. I can't really, it has to go in at the end of the day.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on Stephen Curry's unique shooting motion
quotes.excerpt: I think I have a bit of a classic shot. I get it to Klay, into the pocket and shoot.
quotes.quote: I think I have a bit of a classic shot. I get it to Klay, into the pocket and shoot. What I think you brought to the game is you don't really stop. So like you talked about this shot as a kid, to now it's the same shot but up here. I don't really feel like you stop and if you do it's like the split second.

quotes.speaker: Stephen Curry
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry on his unorthodox off-the-dribble shot
quotes.excerpt: It helped me off the dribble because it's kind of unorthodox, but it is a one piece shot.
quotes.quote: It helped me off the dribble because it's kind of unorthodox, but it is a one piece shot that no matter if you're really all the way on balance or just off, or if you got it all in the right hand, left hand off the dribble, whatever it is, I kind of can get it here quick enough that I still have all of my power. I don't lose anything through that. So that's helped me, especially at 6'3 in the league. No matter who's in front of you, you really feel like I have a chance as long as I get them to drop their hands a little bit, I can get it up there quick and I don't want to have any wasted motion.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on Stephen Curry's range and mechanics
quotes.excerpt: Instead of stopping and having to use all your legs, you're using it all in one motion.
quotes.quote: I also feel like that is a part of your range is that you like instead of stopping and having to use all your legs, you're using it all in one motion. So like he just kept backing up and it's like where's this going? And it's like a flick.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on Stephen Curry's shooting mechanics
quotes.excerpt: It's like a flick. Like I got an opportunity to see this last summer.
quotes.quote: It's like a flick. Like I got an opportunity to see this last summer, first time I was joining forces. I got to see it after practice every day, just like a flick. It didn't matter, you know, certain guys in our league, certain, you know, basketball players all over the world, they have to get in a certain pocket in order for them to even get to here or how, it's like when he touched the ball, by the time he does what he needs to here, it doesn't matter where it's coming from, it come from here, come from here, quick, quick, quick.
